title: Dallas private jet charter
description: Arrange business jet charter from Dallas with EXJET. Compare Love Field and Addison, explore routes and pricing, and request a complete trip proposal.

sections.heading: Charter planning from Dallas–Fort Worth
paragraphs: EXJET is a Dallas-based air charter brokerage arranging flights through licensed third-party operators. Begin with your itinerary, the passenger group and the destination address. We can discuss aircraft options and coordinate the commercial details around those requirements.

The right airport depends on where the travelers start, the proposed aircraft and the onward journey. Give the advisor a pickup address or neighborhood instead of selecting an airport purely by familiarity.

sections.heading: Love Field or Addison?
paragraphs: Dallas Love Field and Addison are useful starting points for a business aviation airport comparison. Love Field combines commercial and general aviation facilities; Addison is a general aviation airport. The operating carrier confirms suitability for the aircraft and mission.

rows: Central Dallas access; exact FBO entrance; complete return itinerary
North Dallas-area destinations; private terminal; customs arrangements if needed

sections.heading: Popular itinerary examples
paragraphs: Compare a few different mission profiles before requesting a quote. A short Houston business trip is often influenced by minimum charges; a New York itinerary needs time-zone and ground-transfer planning; an Aspen visit needs mountain-airport flexibility.

sections.heading: Aircraft and pricing
paragraphs: Specify passenger numbers and bag sizes first, including golf clubs, skis or equipment. Compare the offered cabin layouts and confirm connectivity if it matters to the trip. Published category examples explain the cost calculation; your written quote establishes the actual trip total.

sections.heading: Request Dallas aircraft charter
paragraphs: Send the departure date, destination, passenger count, return or onward sectors and latest useful arrival time. Tell us what is flexible. EXJET can then discuss aircraft sourcing, airport choices and the terms of a specific proposal.

faqs.question: Does EXJET operate the aircraft?
faqs.answer: EXJET is a broker. Flights are provided by the licensed third-party direct air carrier identified for the itinerary.

faqs.question: Can I depart from Addison instead of Love Field?
faqs.answer: You can request either airport. The operator must confirm the proposed aircraft’s suitability and the required handling arrangements; compare both against your pickup address.

faqs.question: Do you guarantee a four-hour departure?
faqs.answer: Departure timing depends on aircraft, crew, airports and the route. Contact EXJET for an urgent request so the operating carrier can confirm a realistic timeline.

title: Dallas empty leg flights
description: Request Dallas empty leg charter opportunities with flexible dates and routing. Understand availability, terms and backup options before confirming with EXJET.

sections.heading: What a Dallas empty leg means
paragraphs: An empty leg is an aircraft repositioning without its primary passenger group. If the operator offers that movement for charter, another traveler may be able to use the available routing and window. The opportunity depends on the underlying aircraft schedule and may change.
This page is an enquiry guide, not a live inventory list. EXJET must reconfirm the actual aircraft, airports, timing and commercial terms before an offer can be accepted.

sections.heading: Make flexibility useful
paragraphs: List the dates and departure windows you can use, which Dallas-area airports are acceptable and how close the destination must be to your final address. Keep passenger and baggage requirements explicit. A discount is only useful if the available routing still meets the purpose of the trip.

sections.heading: Confirm the conditions before paying
paragraphs: Ask what happens if the underlying flight changes, whether any refund or replacement rights apply under the written contract, and what an alternative arrangement would cost. An essential meeting or an international connection may justify a separately sourced charter with more appropriate terms.

sections.heading: Send a matching request
paragraphs: Include Dallas Love Field or Addison if either is practical, your destination and the full flexibility window. EXJET can check current opportunities and compare any match with an on-demand option.

title: Charter safety and operator review
description: Understand operator authority, aircraft verification and independent safety reports. Learn what to confirm before booking business jet charter through EXJET.

sections.heading: Know who operates the flight
paragraphs: EXJET arranges charter as a broker and does not exercise operational control of aircraft. The licensed direct air carrier is responsible for the operation. A proposal should make the operating relationship clear, and the final aircraft and crew details should be confirmed through the agreed process.

sections.heading: Check the operator and the aircraft
paragraphs: For a U.S. Part 135 charter, the FAA publishes a searchable operator and authorized-aircraft list. Check the operating company and the specific registration, rather than treating the FAA ownership registry as proof of charter authority. If a name or aircraft is absent or unclear, follow the FAA’s direction to verify with the appropriate Flight Standards office.

sections.heading: Use independent reports in context
paragraphs: ARGUS and WYVERN provide industry due-diligence and assessment services. An operator’s rating and a trip-specific aircraft-and-crew report answer different questions. Confirm the program, currency and scope relevant to the offered flight. An operator’s rating is not a certification held by EXJET.

sections.heading: Ask for a complete flight brief
paragraphs: Before committing, review the operating carrier, aircraft description, insurance information as applicable, the commercial agreement and the process for a substitution. State any client-specific requirements early so they can be considered during sourcing.
bullets: Identify the direct air carrier and authority appropriate to the trip.

sections.heading: Understand the difference between charter and a lease
paragraphs: A lease that makes a passenger responsible for operating an aircraft is not equivalent to buying a charter flight. Do not assume that a commercial pilot certificate or an attractive aircraft listing alone establishes lawful charter authority. Review the FAA’s passenger guidance and obtain qualified advice before accepting unfamiliar lease obligations.

sources.label: FAA — certificated Part 135 operators and authorized aircraft

title: Part 135 vs Part 91: a charter passenger guide
description: Understand the distinction between on-demand charter and private aircraft operations. Learn what operating authority and aircraft details to verify before booking.

sections.heading: The difference starts with the operation
paragraphs: Part 91 contains general operating rules used for many private flights. Part 135 sets operating requirements for commuter and on-demand operations within its scope. A flight is not classified simply by aircraft model or whether the cabin looks like a business jet.

Ordinary U.S. on-demand paid passenger charter generally requires an appropriately authorized operator, commonly under Part 135. Other operating frameworks and exceptions exist, so the facts of the actual arrangement matter.

sections.heading: A pilot certificate is not an operator certificate
paragraphs: A commercial or airline transport pilot qualification does not by itself authorize a person or company to sell any aircraft flight to the public. The FAA tells passengers to examine the operating company’s authority and the aircraft’s authorization for charter.

sections.heading: A dry lease changes the responsibilities
paragraphs: A true dry lease supplies an aircraft without crew and brings operational-control responsibilities that are different from booking a charter. The FAA warns about arrangements in which the provider supplies aircraft and crew while attempting to transfer control to a passenger through paperwork. Get qualified advice before accepting those responsibilities.

sections.heading: What to check for a proposed charter
paragraphs: Ask for the legal operating company, its certificate information and the aircraft registration. Use the FAA’s operator-and-aircraft resource for a U.S. Part 135 proposal, and resolve discrepancies with the operator and regulator. A registered owner record alone does not establish authorization for the proposed charter.

sections.heading: Keep the decision tied to your flight
paragraphs: If the aircraft or operator changes, ask for the revised information and applicable terms. For international travel, the authority appropriate to the countries and operation must also be considered. This is a passenger orientation, not a determination that an individual contract or flight is lawful.

title: ARGUS and WYVERN safety ratings explained
description: Learn how operator ratings, audits and trip-specific reports differ. Understand what ARGUS and WYVERN information can tell you about a proposed charter flight.

sections.heading: Two different questions to ask
paragraphs: First establish the operator’s legal authority for the flight. Then ask what additional assessment or due-diligence information is available. Independent programs can support that second question, but their ratings do not replace the regulator’s operating authorization.

sections.heading: ARGUS operator assessments
paragraphs: ARGUS describes an operator-rating program that combines data review with differing audit and monitoring requirements across its program levels. Ask for the current designation and what it covers. A logo on a website is less useful than current information for the operating company involved in your flight.

sections.heading: WYVERN and PASS reports
paragraphs: WYVERN distinguishes its audited Wingman program from Registered status and offers PASS reports with different standards and scope. Ask which report is available, what it checks and whether it relates to the actual proposed aircraft and crew.

sections.heading: Operator-level status is not the whole itinerary
paragraphs: A company-wide assessment and a flight-specific report are different evidence. The aircraft, crew assignment, insurance and operating details may change between the initial enquiry and departure. Confirm how changes will be communicated and whether updated review information is needed.

sections.heading: What EXJET represents
paragraphs: EXJET is an air charter broker. We do not present a carrier’s ARGUS or WYVERN standing as a certification held by EXJET. Discuss any requirement for a particular program or report in the request so it can be considered when aircraft are sourced.

sections.heading: Confirm the complete proposal

title: Aircraft charter glossary
description: Understand aircraft charter terms including FBO, block time, positioning, empty legs and operational control. Use EXJET’s glossary to review your next proposal.

sections.heading: Air charter broker
paragraphs: An intermediary that arranges charter with an operating carrier. EXJET acts in this role and does not exercise operational control of aircraft.

sections.heading: Direct air carrier
paragraphs: The company authorized to operate the transportation. Identify the actual carrier for the itinerary, not only the broker or aircraft owner.

sections.heading: FBO
paragraphs: A fixed-base operator: an airport business providing aviation services. Your charter itinerary should identify the exact facility and passenger entrance.

sections.heading: Block time
paragraphs: An elapsed flight-time measure that includes movement before takeoff and after landing. Billing definitions vary, so use the definition in the proposal.

sections.heading: Positioning
paragraphs: Flying an aircraft to meet the passenger itinerary or to its next assignment. The associated charge may be included in the quoted trip total.

sections.heading: Empty leg
paragraphs: A repositioning flight offered for charter when the aircraft would otherwise travel without its primary passengers. Timing and routing depend on the underlying schedule.

sections.heading: Minimum flight charge
paragraphs: A minimum amount of flying billed for a day or sector under an operator’s commercial terms, even if the passenger flight is shorter.

sections.heading: ICAO and IATA codes
paragraphs: Airport identifiers used in aviation and passenger travel. Confirm the exact airport; cities may have several airports and identifiers can change.

sections.heading: Payload
paragraphs: The load carried by the aircraft, including passengers and baggage as applicable. It affects the operating carrier’s performance and range assessment.

sections.heading: Operational control
paragraphs: Responsibility for initiating, conducting and terminating a flight. A passenger charter and an aircraft lease can allocate responsibilities differently.

sections.heading: Aircraft substitution
paragraphs: Replacement of the initially proposed aircraft. The contract should state the process and any conditions or rights that apply.

sections.heading: Trip total
paragraphs: The complete amount proposed for the specified itinerary, with included, excluded and conditional charges identified. It is more useful for comparison than an hourly headline.

sections.heading: Put the terms into context
paragraphs: Use the pricing and operator-review guides when assessing a real proposal, and ask your advisor to explain any term that changes the cost or your responsibilities.

title: Private jet charter for executive assistants
seoTitle: Private jet charter for executive assistants | EXJET
description: Coordinate executive aircraft charter with a clear brief, approval checklist and flight handoff. Plan business travel and request an EXJET proposal.

sections.heading: A practical charter desk for EAs and chiefs of staff
paragraphs: An executive assistant booking a business jet needs a usable proposal, an accountable approval process and a clear itinerary. Begin with the meeting commitment, then work backward through the ground transfer, arrival buffer and flight. EXJET arranges charter through operating carriers; the proposed operator and aircraft should be identified before acceptance.
Use this page as your booking workflow. The detailed checklist linked below covers the information to collect before the first request. Neither an enquiry nor a search result reserves an aircraft.

sections.heading: Give your advisor a brief that supports a decision
paragraphs: Send the business constraints first. Separate a hard arrival deadline from a preferred departure time, and identify whether the return is fixed or dependent on a meeting. For a multi-city itinerary, give the local date and time for every stop.

sections.heading: Present comparable options to your executive
paragraphs: Put each proposal into the same format: aircraft and registration if assigned, operator, flight and ground schedule, complete price, exclusions, cancellation terms and change process. Record any assumption that is still awaiting confirmation. A lower hourly rate is not automatically a lower trip cost.

For a working flight, ask for current cabin images, a seating plan, usable table positions, power and the installed Wi-Fi service. A fleet brochure is not confirmation that the quoted aircraft has that cabin or connection.

sections.heading: Keep the day-of-flight handoff simple
paragraphs: Share one controlled itinerary with the assistant covering the trip, the passenger contact and the approved travel team. Include the exact FBO name and street address, local departure time, ground transport contact and the number to call for a change. Distribute revised versions when anything material changes.

If an executive’s meeting runs late, contact the trip team before promising a new departure. Crew duty, airport restrictions and the aircraft’s next commitments can limit a change. Ask for the revised cost and itinerary before approving it.

sections.heading: Connect your regular business markets
paragraphs: For Dallas departures, compare Love Field and Addison against the office address and aircraft. New York trips should compare the final Manhattan or regional destination with Teterboro access. For South Florida and Los Angeles, give the residence or meeting address before selecting Opa-locka or Van Nuys.

faqs.question: Can EXJET help an EA book without a jet card?
faqs.answer: You can request an on-demand charter proposal for a specific itinerary. Availability, payment and cancellation conditions are set out in the accepted quote and agreement.

faqs.question: What should an EA verify before confirming a flight?
faqs.answer: Verify the operator, aircraft, passenger and baggage requirements, complete price, approved schedule and contract terms. Obtain written confirmation of any essential cabin amenity.

title: Family office private aviation and charter
seoTitle: Family office private aviation and charter | EXJET
description: Plan family office aircraft charter around principals, guests, privacy, cabin needs and approvals. Compare flight options and discuss your itinerary with EXJET.

sections.heading: One aviation brief for a complex household
paragraphs: Family office aviation planning often combines business commitments, household travel and guests on different schedules. Start by identifying who is travelling, who may approve a flight and which requirements are essential. EXJET can discuss on-demand charter sourcing for a particular mission alongside an existing aircraft or aviation program.

The right comparison is the complete journey: cabin suitability, airport access, timing, commercial terms and the process for changes. A larger aircraft is not automatically the better choice for a short trip; an overnight sector may justify a different cabin even with the same passenger count.

sections.heading: Build a passenger profile with permission
paragraphs: Maintain a concise approved profile rather than repeatedly circulating a full personal dossier. Discuss the appropriate channel for passenger identity details and international documents. Limit distribution to those arranging or operating the trip. Do not place passport numbers, medical details or sensitive itineraries in an initial general enquiry.
bullets: Record seating, mobility and boarding requirements that affect aircraft selection.
Describe bags by dimensions and approximate weight; include sports equipment and strollers.
Confirm pet acceptance and any required travel documentation with the operator.
Separate must-have features from preferences, including sleeping arrangements and catering.

sections.heading: Plan for principals, family members and guests
paragraphs: A cabin’s advertised passenger capacity is not its sleeping capacity. Ask for a layout that shows which seats berth, whether sleeping areas can be separated and how the lavatory and baggage space are accessed. Children, support staff and guests should be included in the actual headcount.

For a multi-generational journey, discuss the aircraft entrance, steps, aisle and lavatory layout before accepting a proposal. Confirm assistance arrangements for the specific aircraft and handling facility rather than relying on a model’s cabin width alone.

sections.heading: Separate approval and allocation from the travel experience
paragraphs: Identify the contracting entity, invoice recipient and approver before booking. Where several households or business entities share an itinerary, agree how the office will allocate the expense internally. Your accounting and legal advisors should determine the appropriate treatment; the flight quote is a commercial record, not a tax conclusion.

Keep the accepted proposal, revisions, passenger changes and final invoice together. If the office uses an owned aircraft, fractional share or membership, compare charter as a mission-specific alternative or supplement against the current agreement.

sections.heading: Plan the destination as well as the flight
paragraphs: For Dallas, New York, Palm Beach, Miami and Los Angeles, begin with the residence or meeting address. Seasonal trips to Aspen or Cabo add baggage, airport and international planning questions. Ask early about peak dates and acceptable alternatives; availability is confirmed for the itinerary.

faqs.question: Does a family office need to own an aircraft to use EXJET?
faqs.answer: No. A family office can request a charter proposal for a specific trip. EXJET is a broker, and the operating carrier provides the aircraft, crew and flight operation.

faqs.question: Can one aircraft accommodate a family’s seating and sleeping needs?
faqs.answer: Possibly, but the specific cabin configuration must be checked. Ask separately about approved passenger seats, sleeping positions, baggage and access requirements.

title: Private aviation planning for Fortune 500 travel teams
seoTitle: Private aviation planning for Fortune 500 travel teams | EXJET
description: A charter planning framework for Fortune 500 travel teams: approvals, operator review, executive scheduling and supplemental lift. Build an EXJET trip brief.

sections.heading: Start with the travel policy and business requirement
paragraphs: Large-company aviation procurement involves more than choosing an aircraft. The travel team needs a documented business purpose, an authorized buyer, a clear operating-carrier relationship and a practical process for changes. This guide is for teams at Fortune 500 and other enterprise businesses; it is not a claim that EXJET serves any named company.

Define the mission first: board travel, a site visit, several same-day meetings or a flight-department capacity gap. Record the arrival deadline and consequence of delay, then consider scheduled airline service, existing corporate lift and a charter proposal on the same door-to-door basis.

sections.heading: Build an approval path before requesting lift
paragraphs: Identify who can approve the spend, sign the agreement and authorize a change after hours. Your company’s procurement, risk and legal teams should specify the evidence they require. A broker should not be asked to make your company’s internal policy decision.

sections.heading: Coordinate with the corporate flight department
paragraphs: When charter supplements an existing fleet, let the flight department define acceptable aircraft categories, operator-review requirements and operational constraints. Keep the executive office, sourcing team and flight department aligned on which aircraft is primary and whether alternatives are actually confirmed.

A charter request is not a standby aircraft commitment. If the business requires backup capacity, specify the period, location, readiness expectations and commercial terms and obtain a written proposal.

sections.heading: Plan roadshows around meetings and recovery time
paragraphs: For several cities, map each meeting address and latest useful arrival. Include transfers, boarding, servicing and a realistic buffer. An itinerary that appears possible from airborne times alone can fail when a meeting overruns. Ask the operator to assess feasibility before the team commits to the schedule.

sections.heading: Review completed trips against useful measures
paragraphs: Track quote-to-approval time, changes after acceptance, final cost against the approved proposal and the reasons for exceptions. Record whether the itinerary met the business requirement. These measures help refine future briefs without inventing a savings percentage or treating every flight hour as an interchangeable product.

title: Corporate jet charter procurement checklist
seoTitle: Corporate jet charter procurement checklist | EXJET
description: Compare charter proposals with a practical procurement checklist covering operator details, aircraft, total cost, approvals and change terms for executive travel.

sections.heading: Compare the same trip before comparing price
paragraphs: A useful procurement comparison holds the itinerary, passenger needs and service requirements constant. Put each proposed departure, arrival, aircraft category and inclusion into one record. If one quote uses a different airport or time window, flag that difference beside its price.

Ask for a complete trip total and an explanation of conditional charges. Positioning, minimum billable time, overnight crew costs, handling and weather-related services can change the result. Do not treat a manufacturer’s aircraft operating-cost estimate as a charter retail price.

sections.heading: Request a proposal that can be approved
paragraphs: Use the following checklist to expose unanswered questions before the agreement is accepted.
bullets: Who is the contracting party, and which carrier will operate the flight?
What aircraft type and variant are proposed, and when is its registration assigned?
What is included in the quoted total, and which charges remain conditional?
What payment deadlines and cancellation conditions apply?
What happens if the aircraft changes or becomes unavailable?
Which cabin, connectivity and passenger requirements are confirmed in writing?
Who can approve a change, and who is reachable during travel?

sections.heading: Keep operator review distinct from aircraft selection
paragraphs: Review the operating entity and relevant evidence against your organization’s policy. A rating or database entry is not proof that a particular tail is available or authorized for the proposed mission. Ask the trip team to resolve mismatched names, expired documents or unclear aircraft information before confirmation.

sections.heading: Document exceptions and changes
paragraphs: If the executive accepts an alternative airport or cabin, record that decision with the revised itinerary and cost. Keep a clear version of the accepted proposal rather than relying on several disconnected messages. After the flight, compare the invoice against that version and reconcile adjustments.

For recurring travel, use the same comparison headings across trips. Trends in positioning, overnight fees or frequently revised return times can reveal where a different itinerary or aviation arrangement deserves review.

title: Supplemental aircraft charter for corporate travel
seoTitle: Supplemental aircraft charter for corporate travel | EXJET
description: Plan supplemental charter when a corporate aircraft or aviation program cannot cover the mission. Define cabin needs, operator review and backup expectations.

sections.heading: What is supplemental lift?
paragraphs: Supplemental lift is aircraft capacity sourced in addition to an existing aviation arrangement. A business may need it during scheduled maintenance, overlapping executive trips or a mission that exceeds its usual aircraft’s cabin or range. A family office may need a second aircraft when principals travel separately.

On-demand charter can be considered for these gaps, but availability and terms must be confirmed for the specific itinerary. An open enquiry or an example aircraft page is not a reservation or recovery guarantee.

sections.heading: Describe the gap before selecting a substitute
paragraphs: Tell EXJET why the usual aircraft cannot serve the trip and which capabilities need to be preserved. A familiar category name may conceal differences in baggage, seating, cabin systems or international capability.

table.caption: Supplemental-lift scenarios
rows: Known dates, flexibility and required travel windows
Separate passenger lists, destinations and approval contacts
Payload, rest needs and whether a fuel stop is acceptable
Actual seats required, baggage and ground coordination
Current location, earliest practical departure and alternatives

sections.heading: Agree the substitution process
paragraphs: Ask how a proposed aircraft change will be communicated and approved. Specify essential cabin features and the acceptable category range, but avoid promising passengers an exact tail until it is assigned and confirmed. Reconfirm the operator and trip particulars if a substitution occurs.

For time-critical travel, discuss airport alternatives, schedule flexibility and the commercial terms of any dedicated standby arrangement. Backup capacity is a separate commitment that needs explicit agreement.

sections.heading: Connect the flight department and the assistant
paragraphs: The flight department can define technical review criteria while the EA maintains the executive’s schedule. Nominate one point of contact for acceptance and one for operational updates. Keep the same local-time convention and current passenger brief across all parties.

title: Multi-city private jet charter for executive roadshows
seoTitle: Multi-city private jet charter for executive roadshows | EXJET
description: Plan executive roadshows and multi-city charter with meeting buffers, airport choices, passenger changes and clear approvals. Discuss your schedule with EXJET.

sections.heading: Build the schedule around the meetings
paragraphs: A multi-city charter itinerary should begin with meeting addresses and required arrival times. For an investor roadshow, board visit or portfolio-company tour, list the business commitments in order before selecting airports. EXJET can discuss aircraft sourcing once the trip’s constraints are clear.

Do not build a day by adding flight times alone. Ground transfers, boarding, handling, fuel, crew requirements and the possibility of a delayed meeting all affect feasibility. The operating carrier must assess the actual schedule.

sections.heading: Label every time and every passenger change
paragraphs: Use local dates and airport time zones for each sector. State whether passengers remain with the aircraft or change between stops. A stop that adds colleagues can change payload and baggage requirements for the next leg.

For a Dallas–New York–South Florida sequence, give each meeting address and explain whether the final arrival is in Miami or Palm Beach. Those are different destination requirements. A later meeting finish should trigger a revised schedule, not an assumed extension.

sections.heading: Compare waiting with repositioning
paragraphs: Ask how the proposal treats aircraft waiting time, crew overnights and any repositioning between sectors. A single aircraft for the entire itinerary may simplify the passenger experience, but the quote must explain the commercial and operational assumptions.

If different aircraft are proposed for different legs, compare the cabin and baggage limitations for each one. Identify where passengers would need to transfer belongings and who coordinates the handoff.

sections.heading: Define a change decision before the day begins
paragraphs: Assign an approver who can decide whether to shorten a meeting, change an airport, accept a revised price or move a leg. Agree how passengers receive the current itinerary. Preserve a realistic buffer around the most important commitment instead of distributing every minute across optional stops.

title: Family office flight planning checklist
seoTitle: Family office flight planning checklist | EXJET
description: Prepare a family office charter brief covering household needs, seating, sleeping, baggage, approvals and destination transfers for principals and guests.

sections.heading: Separate the household brief from the passenger manifest
paragraphs: The first enquiry needs the itinerary, headcount and requirements that affect aircraft selection. Personal identity documents and sensitive information should be shared only through the channel agreed for the trip and with the parties who need them. Keep one authorized office contact responsible for updates.

sections.heading: Create a cabin brief for the actual travelling party
paragraphs: List adults, children, accompanying staff and guests in the passenger count. Describe whether people need to work, dine or sleep at the same time. For an overnight journey, count usable sleeping positions separately from seats. Ask how the specific aircraft is configured.

Measure unusual baggage before choosing a cabin: ski bags, golf clubs, strollers and larger cases may be constrained by compartment shape or the baggage door. Published volume alone does not establish that an item will fit.

table.caption: Family-office cabin checklist
rows: Sleeping positions, separation and bedding arrangement
Boarding steps, aisle, lavatory and assistance plan
Acceptance, cabin arrangements and destination documentation

sections.heading: Connect the aircraft to the destination plan
paragraphs: For a coastal stay, confirm the residence or marina address and ground transfer. For a mountain trip, discuss weather flexibility and alternate airports before promising an arrival time. International travel requires an itinerary-specific document and entry review with the appropriate professionals.

Send catering and household preferences early enough for the trip team to confirm what can be supplied. Do not assume a photographed galley, shower or entertainment system is installed on the quoted tail.

sections.heading: Close the approval loop
paragraphs: Keep the office approver, contracting entity, guest contact and invoice recipient clear. Record what the family accepted and which items remain pending. If a tail changes, check the cabin and passenger requirements again rather than treating the replacement as identical.

title: Executive charter airport planning by business market
seoTitle: Executive charter airport planning by business market | EXJET
description: Compare Dallas, New York, Miami, Palm Beach and Los Angeles airport choices by meeting address, FBO handoff and transfer requirements for executive travel.

sections.heading: Choose the airport from the destination address
paragraphs: The airport with the shortest airborne route is not always the most practical arrival point. Compare the meeting or residence address, expected ground journey, handling arrangements and the operating carrier’s assessment of aircraft suitability. Ask for the exact FBO and address on the confirmed itinerary.

The markets below are planning starting points, not statements that EXJET has offices or based aircraft in each location. Current airport restrictions, handling capacity and aircraft availability need trip-specific confirmation.

sections.heading: Dallas: Love Field and Addison
paragraphs: For Dallas executive travel, compare Dallas Love Field (KDAL/DAL) and Addison (KADS/ADS) against the office or residence. North Dallas and central Dallas have different ground journeys. Share the destination address and acceptable departure window before choosing the airport.

sections.heading: New York: specify Manhattan or the wider region
paragraphs: Teterboro (KTEB/TEB) is a useful starting point for New York business-aviation planning, but the final address matters. Build transfer time and meeting buffer into the decision. Ask for the current operating restrictions and handling arrangements for the offered aircraft rather than assuming every requested time is usable.

sections.heading: South Florida: Miami and Palm Beach are separate missions
paragraphs: For a Miami destination, discuss Miami-Opa locka Executive (KOPF/OPF) with the trip team. For Palm Beach, begin with the Palm Beach destination guide. A family office moving between residences should specify each address instead of treating all South Florida airports as interchangeable.

sections.heading: Los Angeles: plan the ground journey
paragraphs: For a Los Angeles business trip, compare Van Nuys (KVNY/VNY) with the actual meeting schedule and destination. Ground travel can dominate a tightly planned day. Give the trip team enough time to assess alternatives and confirm which facility passengers should use.

sections.heading: What belongs on the final itinerary
paragraphs: Include the airport code, FBO name, street address, local departure time, passenger arrival instructions and ground-transport contact. When an airport changes, update every downstream arrangement and distribute one revised itinerary.

title: How to verify a charter aircraft tail number
seoTitle: How to verify a charter aircraft tail number | EXJET
description: Use a charter aircraft tail number to verify the proposed model, operator and cabin. Learn why database records and published specs do not confirm availability.

sections.heading: What a tail number tells you
paragraphs: A tail number is an aircraft registration identifier. It helps distinguish a specific airframe from the general aircraft model named in a proposal. It does not by itself establish current charter availability, the installed cabin or authorization for your itinerary. Registrations and operating arrangements can change.

For a useful comparison, ask the trip team to connect the registration, exact type and variant, operating carrier and current cabin details in the same proposal. Do not transfer specifications between similar names such as a Global 6000 and Global 7500 or a Citation Latitude and Longitude.

sections.heading: Use database records as a starting point
paragraphs: An operator directory or fleet spreadsheet can help identify aircraft types to research. Its date, coverage and verification limits matter. A historical base is not proof that the aircraft is positioned there today, and a company-level safety rating should not be presented as an individual airframe guarantee.

EXJET’s aircraft performance guides describe the type using manufacturer references. They do not publish a live fleet or promise a particular registration. Current charter suitability must be checked for the actual proposal.

sections.heading: Ask for aircraft-specific evidence
paragraphs: Before accepting an aircraft, resolve the details that matter to the passengers and the organization’s approval process.
bullets: Exact model and variant associated with the proposed registration.
Operating carrier and the trip team’s current operator-review evidence.
Recent aircraft-specific cabin photographs and seating layout.
Installed Wi-Fi, sleeping positions, lavatory and baggage configuration.
Written confirmation of passenger, baggage and itinerary suitability.
The procedure for approval if the aircraft or operator changes.

sections.heading: Read performance numbers in context
paragraphs: Manufacturer range, maximum speed and maximum passenger capacity are different measurements. They are not necessarily achievable together. Range figures use stated assumptions for passengers, crew, reserves and speed; a full cabin or stronger headwind can change the mission.

The operating carrier evaluates the route, conditions and aircraft. A brochure takeoff distance is not a passenger-facing runway approval. Use the figures to compare types, then obtain a mission assessment.

title: NetJets, Flexjet, VistaJet and charter: what to compare
seoTitle: NetJets, Flexjet, VistaJet and charter: what to compare | EXJET
description: Compare private aviation programs and on-demand charter by commitment, trip cost, aircraft fit and terms. A practical buying framework for EAs and family offices.

sections.heading: Compare the access model before the brand
paragraphs: NetJets, Flexjet, VistaJet, Air Charter Service and Wheels Up appear in many private-aviation shortlists, but their offerings are not one interchangeable product. Compare the current agreement that fits your travel pattern, then review charter for the same set of missions. EXJET is an independent charter brokerage and is not affiliated with these providers.
This is a purchasing framework, not a price ranking. Program terms change, and an advertised benefit should be checked against the proposal and contract you are actually considering.

sections.heading: What the named providers emphasize
paragraphs: The linked provider pages are starting points for your research. Ask each provider for the currently applicable offering, service area, availability conditions and commercial terms.

rows: Private aviation service and corporate travel support

sections.heading: Use the same representative trips
paragraphs: Select a short domestic trip, a longer sector, an overnight itinerary and a peak-date request from your expected travel. Ask how each proposal treats these missions, including aircraft changes, positioning, minimums, availability and cancellation. Compare the complete annual commitment separately from the cost of a single journey.

For a family office, include seasonal travel and simultaneous trips by different principals. For an enterprise team, include a multi-city day and a supplemental-lift requirement. The result should reveal where each arrangement fits and where another solution may be needed.

sections.heading: Ask questions that expose the tradeoffs
paragraphs: A program may offer consistency while requiring an ongoing commitment. On-demand charter prices and availability depend on the particular trip. Neither model should be selected from an hourly headline alone.
bullets: What money is committed upfront, and what happens to unused funds or hours?
Which dates, aircraft categories and regions have additional conditions?
How are substitutions, recovery and simultaneous aircraft requests handled?
Which costs are included and which are variable?
How much notice is required, and what are the cancellation terms?
Who operates the flight and who handles the booking relationship?

sections.heading: Where an EXJET charter proposal fits
paragraphs: Ask EXJET for an itinerary-specific charter comparison when the trip is occasional, outside an existing arrangement or needs a different cabin. Review the offered operator, aircraft and terms together. This does not imply that charter will always be cheaper or that any provider can guarantee every requested mission.
